subject.title: feat(session): add named new and close chat commands

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `/close` and `/delete` as chat-side destructive session commands now, after the parser fix and proof refresh, or should that capability stay in UI/API session management for this cycle?
rationale: The code bug is mechanical, but adding destructive session mutation from chat changes a user-facing session-state surface and overlaps with active session title/management work, so maintainer product intent is needed before merge.

options.title: Accept after parser and proof fixes
options.body: Land the chat command surface once catalog-backed `/new` model tails fall through, the branch is rebased, and current-head proof shows named-new plus close/delete behavior.

options.title: Wait for session title migration
options.body: Hold this PR until the canonical title migration lands, then rebase and write the approved naming field instead of extending a label-only path.

options.title: Drop destructive chat commands
options.body: Keep named-new work but remove `/close` and `/delete` if maintainers want deletion/archive actions limited to session-management UI/API flows for now.

recommendation.title: Accept after parser and proof fixes
recommendation.body: Land the chat command surface once catalog-backed `/new` model tails fall through, the branch is rebased, and current-head proof shows named-new plus close/delete behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this account to session lifecycle, reset-model selection, and cross-surface session controls affected by the product decision.
